# Web front end

## Scope

Applies when the change touches HTML, CSS, browser code. Not when the screen is a native mobile app, or the change is server-only. Neighbours: `aidd-team:accessible-ui`, `aidd-team:prototyping`, `aidd-team:product-defaults`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Open choices

The team decides these. aidd's default holds until a `[[standards]]` entry fills one (`aidd standard list`).

| Choice | Question | aidd's default | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web-framework` | Which framework renders the web front end? | The framework the app already uses. For a new app, one that renders on the server and meets the browser support target. | Next.js, React Router, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Astro, Angular |
| `e2e-test` | Which runner drives a real browser for end-to-end tests? | Playwright (`@playwright/test`), which the browser checks of `aidd-team:accessible-ui` and `aidd-team:product-defaults` also run. | Playwright, Cypress, WebdriverIO |
| `component-test` | Which library tests a component the way a person uses it? | Testing Library for the web framework in use, run by the project's test runner. | Testing Library, Vitest browser mode, Cypress component testing, Storybook interaction tests |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd assess`) | Name the pages, components, and states the change touches; a user-facing change needs the product designer and `design.files`. | S1 |
| Entry (`aidd assess`) | Product defaults (`dark_mode`, `responsive`, `i18n_ready`, `perf_budget`, `public_page_basics`, `legal_placeholders`, `transactional_email`, `security_headers`): build each one `[project.defaults] off` does not name, as `aidd-team:product-defaults` says. | — |
| Specify | Acceptance names every state per screen (empty, loading, error, partial, success, offline) and the keyboard path through it. | S1 |
| Specify | The browser support target is Baseline Widely available (or a named Baseline year) in the Spec; a feature outside it has a fallback. | S6 |
| Specify | Consent: no non-essential cookie, storage, or tracker before consent where ePrivacy Art. 5(3) applies; a Global Privacy Control signal is honoured as an opt-out where a US state law requires it (`aidd-team:privacy-by-default` names which). | S8 |
| Implement | Semantic HTML first, ARIA only where HTML has no element; focus order and a visible focus ring preserved. | S1 |
| Implement | No inline script and no `unsafe-inline`: nonces or hashes under the CSP. Every third-party script named in the Spec and pinned with `integrity` (SRI). A `Permissions-Policy` turns off the features the page does not use. | S3, S7 |
| Review | Untrusted strings reach the DOM only through escaping or a sanitizer, with Trusted Types enforced (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`) where the engines support it; URLs are validated before `href` or `src`. | S4, S3 |
| Ship | Core Web Vitals field data and the client error rate are the observe signals. | S2 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSP evaluation | no `unsafe-inline` and no wildcard source in the policy | Google CSP Evaluator or a lint step in CI | S3 |
| ESLint with jsx-a11y and security plugins | no accessibility or injection anti-pattern in the code | `eslint` with `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@6.10.2` and `eslint-plugin-security@4.1.0`, in the test commands | S1, S4 |
| Design-token lint | no raw colour, size, or space outside the repository's design tokens | `stylelint@17.15.0` with `color-no-hex` and the `stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.12.1` plugin's `scale-unlimited/declaration-strict-value` on colour properties; ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` on a literal colour in a JSX `style` object | S5 |
| Browser support check | no API outside the Baseline target without a fallback | `eslint-plugin-compat` (7.0.2) with the browserslist query `baseline widely available` (browserslist 4.29.3), in the lint step | S6 |
| Cookie and tracker consent test | no non-essential cookie, storage, or third-party request before consent, and none after a refusal or a `Sec-GPC: 1` request | the team's `e2e-test` runner, by default `@playwright/test` (1.63.0), in a fresh context: record cookies, storage, and requests before and after each consent choice | S8 |

- From `aidd-team:accessible-ui`: Accessibility per state, Keyboard-only flows.
- From `aidd-team:prototyping`: Screenshot matrix.
- From `aidd-team:product-defaults`: Performance budget, Both themes, Responsive and targets, Security headers.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`. Steward: @thaithienvanid, who reviews every change to this pack's standards.
